subject.title: PR4/5 durable core: wake controls, inspection, CLI, and Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable runtime and its twelve-table shared-state, Gateway protocol, CLI, and SDK surface on the 2026.7.1 release line, or defer it to a main-targeted architecture cycle?
rationale: This is a new core persistence and control-plane architecture rather than a bounded bug fix, and repository policy requires maintainer intent before accepting its long-lived schema, environment, protocol, and ownership contracts.

options.title: Defer to main architecture review
options.body: Pause release-line landing, preserve the inspection-first work, and sponsor a main-targeted stack after exact-head upgrade and runtime proof is complete.

options.title: Sponsor the release stack
options.body: Explicitly accept the new core ownership and release risk, then require the finding fix and full current-head proof matrix before merge.

options.title: Decline durable core
options.body: Close the stack if OpenClaw should continue using existing task, session, audit, delivery-queue, and plugin-owned durability seams instead.

recommendation.title: Defer to main architecture review
recommendation.body: Pause release-line landing, preserve the inspection-first work, and sponsor a main-targeted stack after exact-head upgrade and runtime proof is complete.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to Gateway authorization, control-plane architecture, and core runtime ownership decisions.
